characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Instron 5967 screw driven tensile testing machine
characterization_methods.key_findings: 750 °C, 60 min: YS = 265 MPa, UTS = 394 MPa, uniform elongation = 29.8%, yield ratio 0.67.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; sub-size specimen gauge 6 mm × 2 mm parallel to RD; 3 tests per condition
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine yield strength, UTS and elongation of the annealed samples

characterization_methods.key_findings: Equiaxed, fully recrystallised grains; grain size = 48.3 ± 1.2 µm for 750 °C/60 min (grain growth relative to 25.2 ± 5.0 µm at 5 min).
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine ferrite grain size of the annealed samples

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: X-Pert PRO diffractometer with Cu-Kα radiation; (110) peak used; MAUD Rietveld refinement; ANIZC for dislocation contrast factor
characterization_methods.key_findings: For 750 °C, 60 min: micro-strain = 1.46 × 10^-4; dislocation density ~1 × 10^12 m^-2; ferrite phase confirmed.
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine crystallite size, micro-strain, lattice parameter and dislocation density of ferrite
characterization_methods.technique: XRD line profile analysis (Variance / restricted-moment method of Wilson and Groma)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: conventional constant acceleration Doppler velocity drive with 57Co (Rh-matrix) source; velocity calibrated with pure α-Fe foil; NORMOS fitting
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe-6.8Al spectrum deconvoluted into five B_hf components (32.68, 30.34, 27.69, 25.05, 23.26 T) with volume fractions 7.7, 44, 24.8, 2.6 and 1.4% respectively; low-intensity ~23 T component indicates a possible Fe3Al phase with low volume fraction.
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine local atomic configurations and detect ordered Fe3Al phase

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: laboratory-based dual energy Mo-Cr-SAXS system (Xeuss, Xenocs, France); FIT2D software; glassy carbon secondary standard; silver-behenate calibration
characterization_methods.key_findings: Nano-sized ordered phase scattering peak at q = 0.3–3 nm^-1; Fe3Al ordered-phase diameter increases from 2.5 ± 0.15 nm to 3.75 ± 0.2 nm with increasing Al content (5–9 wt%).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: transmission geometry, q-range 0.0254–10 nm^-1, camera lengths 550 and 2400 mm, 4–6 h per profile (powder sample)
characterization_methods.purpose: Quantify size and volume fraction of nano-sized ordered Fe3Al phase

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: twin jet electropolishing sample preparation (78% methanol, 10% lactic acid, 7% sulfuric acid, 3% nitric acid, 2% hydrochloric acid)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Very fine ordered phase (bright) in dark background; weak superlattice spots; ordered phase size = 2.1 ± 0.2 nm, in correlation with the SAXS estimate.
characterization_methods.purpose: Detect and image the ordered phase and superlattice reflections
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM): dark-field imaging and selected-area electron diffraction

analytical_models.model_note: τ_ss calculated as 95.6 MPa for the Fe-6.8Al alloy.
τ_PN ~154.34 MPa at 0 K; a room-temperature value of 41 MPa (Speich and Swann for 0.4 wt% C steel) was used for the analysis.
Ordered phase size/volume fraction determined by TEM (2.1 ± 0.2 nm) and SAXS.
k_HP for 99.95% pure iron (Refs. [49,50]) used; ferrite grain size from SEM.
Dislocation density determined by the XRD variance method applied to the (110) peak.

computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical modelling of individual strengthening mechanisms to deconstruct the yield strength
computational_details.software_used: MAUD (Rietveld refinement of XRD profiles); ANIZC (dislocation contrast factor); NORMOS (Mössbauer fitting)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Modelled sum of strengthening contributions reproduces the measured yield strength of 265 MPa for the 750 °C, 60 min sample (Fig. 9); error bars associated with grain boundary and ordered phase contributions.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: High angle grain boundaries arrest the motion of dislocations (Hall-Petch strengthening); for the fully recrystallised 60 min sample grain boundary strengthening is the dominant mechanism (contribution up to ~200 MPa in Fig. 9).

In the ordered phase, dislocations travel in pairs (leading dislocation destroys order; trailing restores it), creating an antiphase boundary; splitting into super-partial dislocations increases the flow stress.

interfaces.interface_notes: For the sample annealed 60 min, the major strengthening contributions come from (i) ordering and (ii) solid solution strengthening; grain boundary (~200 MPa) and solid solution remain appreciable contributions to the 265 MPa yield strength.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Ferrite recrystallization is complete within 5 min at 750 °C; annealing to 60 min causes ferrite grain growth (25.2 → 48.3 µm) and a higher extent of ordering.

phase_interfaces.coherence: nano-sized coherent ordered phase formed within the ferrite matrix

interfaces.slip_behavior: Dislocations glide on the slip plane in the ferrite matrix; in the ordered Fe3Al phase dislocations must move in pairs (super-partial dislocations) with an antiphase boundary between them.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Fe-6.8Al alloy cold rolled to 98% reduction in thickness, producing heavily elongated and pancaked grains along the rolling direction and shear bands at ~40° to RD (Ref. [15]).
Annealed at 750 °C for 60 min, leading to recrystallization (completed within 5 min) and subsequent ferrite grain growth; annealing beyond complete recrystallization causes higher extent of ordering.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Uniaxial tensile tests; three tensile tests conducted for each sample condition.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: sub-size tensile specimen, gauge length 6 mm, width 2 mm; gauge section machined parallel to rolling direction (RD)

tensile_properties.strain_hardening_rate: Rate of strain hardening for the 60 min annealed sample is higher than the 5 min sample at all true strains; a sudden increase followed by a gradual decrease with further straining (Fig. 8b).
tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve (Fig. 8a, 60 min / blue): yield ~300 MPa, plateau ~395 MPa, terminating near 38% strain at ~230 MPa.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: 25.2–48.3 µm (grain growth from the 5 min anneal to the 60 min anneal)

precipitates.distribution: very fine ordered phase (bright) associated with dark background, appearing aligned in bands in dark-field TEM

structures.overall_structure: Single ferrite (BCC) phase matrix with nanometre-sized Fe3Al (DO3) ordered phase; equiaxed and fully recrystallised grains, strain-free after annealing at 750 °C for 60 min.

unmapped_findings: Yield ratio (YS/UTS) for the 750 °C, 60 min sample = 0.67 (Table 4), lower than that of the 98% CR sample.
For the sample annealed for 60 min, the contribution from (i) ordering and (ii) solid solution strengthening are the major contributing mechanisms to the yield strength (b0098).
Micro-strain of the 750 °C, 60 min sample = 1.46 × 10^-4 (XRD), a one-order-of-magnitude drop from the 98% CR state (1.46 × 10^-3).

The drastic change in yield strength (1800 MPa for 98% CR to 265 MPa for the 750 °C/60 min anneal) accompanies a dislocation-density change from ~2.2 × 10^15 m^-2 (98% CR) to ~10^12 m^-2 (b0076), identifying dislocation strengthening as a main mechanism.

By Mössbauer spectroscopy the Fe-6.8Al composition shows five hyperfine-field components with B_hf/Area/V_f: 32.68 T (8.55%/7.7%), 30.34 T (45.45%/44%), 27.69 T (23.63%/24.8%), 25.05 T (2.35%/2.6%), 23.26 T (1.26%/1.4%) — the ~23 T component being a possible indicator of a low-volume-fraction Fe3Al phase (Table 1).

Fig. 9 approximate strengthening contributions for the 750 °C/60 min sample (total YS = 265 MPa): lattice frictional stress (small sliver), solid solution ~80 MPa, grain boundary ~200 MPa, thin dislocation band, and an ordering cap completing 265 MPa; error bars associated with grain-boundary and ordered-phase strengthening.

Comparison: Rana et al. [3] reported YS = 342 MPa for Fe-6.8Al annealed at 900 °C for 1 min (ferrite grain size 69.2 ± 34.8 µm), higher than the 265 MPa of this 750 °C/60 min sample, attributed to the higher ferrite grain size in the present case.
The ordered Fe3Al phase size increases with aluminium content; from SAXS it ranges between 2.5 ± 0.15 nm and 3.75 ± 0.2 nm over 5–9 wt% Al (Fig. 4).
